title: Polysome profiling followed by quantitative PCR for identifying potential micropeptide encoding long non-coding RNAs in suspension cell lines
protocol: Grow MV4-11 cells in IMDM modified medium (10% fetal bovine serum) at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Maintain cell density between 1∗10^5 and 1∗10^6 cells/mL.
Treat the cells with 100 μg/mL cycloheximide.
Incubate treated cells in culture flask at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 15 min.
Harvest cells with ice-cold PBS supplemented with 100 μg/mL cycloheximide.
Centrifuge the sample at 500 × g for 3 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cells with ice-cold PBS supplemented with 100 μg/mL cycloheximide.
Centrifuge the cells at 500 × g for 3 min at 4°C.
Repeat the wash step one more time.
Remove the supernatant as much as possible with precaution.
Suspend cell pellets with lysis buffer supplemented with RNase inhibitor, DTT, PMSF, and cycloheximide.
Place the sample on ice for 30 minutes with occasional inverting.
Centrifuge the cell lysate at 13,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new pre-chilled 1.5 mL tube.
Place the tube on ice until use.
Prepare sucrose gradient for density gradient centrifugation while cells are being lysed.
Mark the half-full position with the marker casing tube provided by the gradient maker.
Mix 10% sucrose buffer with a 1 mL pipette until it reaches the half-full position of the ultracentrifuge tube.
Layer 45% sucrose buffer using a long blunt needle until the upper 10% sucrose buffer reaches the top of the tube.
Lid the tube with the rate zonal cap, contacting the sucrose buffer with one side of the cap first and then slowly dropping the other side that has the air hole into the tube.
Ensure the plate that the magnetic tube holder is attached to is level.
Run the sucrose gradient maker by selecting “10%–45%”.
Mix the sucrose solution slowly and gently upon completion of gradient making.
Pause point: Store the prepared sucrose cushion at −80°C for up to 6 months until use if needed.
Lift the cap of the tube.
Layer the cell lysate onto the sucrose cushion using a 200 μl pipette.
Touch the pipette tip to the upper side of the tube.
Dispense the cell lysate slowly and gently to avoid disturbing the sucrose gradient.
Place the sucrose cushion tube loaded with samples into the SW41 rotor bucket.
Use an analytical scale to balance the opposing rotor buckets.
Screw the cap into the bucket.
Hook the buckets onto the rotor hanger.
Arrange the buckets symmetrically on the rotor.
Screw the cap anticlockwise until you hear a click sound.
Screw the cap clockwise until there is metal-to-metal contact.
Lift the rotor with steady hands and install it perpendicularly on the ultracentrifuge drive hub.
Manually turn the rotor clockwise to check for proper installation.
Centrifuge at 36,000 rpm (222,227 × g) for 3 hours at 4°C using SW41 Ti rotor.
Choose speed “5” instead of max deceleration for optimal polysome sedimentation.
Check the ultracentrifuge occasionally to ensure proper functioning.
Turn on the fractionation system 30 minutes before the end of ultracentrifugation.
Switch on pump, UV detector, fractionation collector, and computer.
Press “SCAN” on the control panel to connect the computer successfully.
Check if the fractionation collector is at the initial position.
If not at the initial position, press “END” on the control panel.
Open Triax™ FlowCell software on the computer.
Set parameters for fractionation.
Collect each ribosome-bound RNA fraction for subsequent analysis.
Fill the syringe attached to the fractionation station with DEPC-treated water.
Press “air” on the control panel to remove any residual water.
Repeat the rinse and air operations for two more times.
Prepare 2 ml tubes for collecting fractions.
Place the tubes into the tube rack in order of collection.
Take out the rotor from the ultracentrifuge once the polysome sedimentation ends.
Place the rotor onto the adapter.
Remove the cap of the bucket using a screwdriver.
Retrieve the centrifuge tube with tweezers carefully.
Place the cap of the SW41 tube holder onto the centrifuge tube containing the cell sample.
Fit the cap of the tube holder onto the sample tube.
Install the loaded tube holder onto the fractionation station.
Transfer the loaded tube holder to let it slide into the fractionation station.
Turn the tube holder clockwise to prepare for collection.
Start the run by clicking “START SCAN” in the software program.
Collect each fraction using a piston tip from top to bottom.
Record UV absorbance at 260 nm simultaneously during collection.
Ensure every drop of each fraction is collected into its corresponding 2 mL tube.
Press “Air” when the run ends to blow out residual drops for collection.
Transfer the 2 mL tube onto ice immediately after collection.
Add an equal volume of RNAiso Plus solution to each tube.
Vigorously vortex each tube to mix thoroughly.
Flash freeze each fraction with RNAiso Plus solution in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen fractions at -80°C until use.
Take samples from −80°C and quickly thaw them at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add 0.2 mL of chloroform per 1 mL of RNAiso Plus solution.
Vortex vigorously for 30 s to mix the chloroform thoroughly.
Keep the samples at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 5 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 12,000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Transfer the top layer into new RNase-free 1.5 mL tubes.
Do not touch the middle layer to avoid DNA contamination.
Use two or more tubes for each fraction to ensure the aqueous phase volume is no more than 0.75 mL.
Add equal volumes of ice-cold isopropanol and 1 μL GlycoBlue™ Coprecipitant to the sample.
Mix thoroughly.
Keep the mixture at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 10 minutes to precipitate RNA.
Optional: Keep the mixture at −20°C for at least 1 hour to increase RNA yield.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully discard the supernatant without touching the pellet.
Centrifuge shortly and remove any remaining isopropanol completely.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold 75% ethanol to wash the RNA pellet.
Vortex briefly and centrifuge at 7,500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Do not disperse the pellet during vortexing.
Carefully discard the supernatant after washing with 75% ethanol.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold 100% ethanol to wash the RNA pellet a second time.
Vortex briefly and centrifuge at 7,500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C again.
Centrifuge shortly and remove any remaining ethanol completely.
Air dry the pellet for 5 minutes.
Dissolve the pellet with 10–30 μL RNase-free water.
Maintain the final volume of the RNA solution identical for each fraction of polysome profiling.
Keep the RNA solution on ice for immediate subsequent analyses to prevent degradation.
Store the RNA solution at −80°C if not used immediately, avoiding freeze-thaw cycles.
Measure RNA concentrations by NanoDrop™ 2000 spectrophotometer.
Apply DNase I treatment if genomic DNA elimination is not included in the reverse-transcription step.
Reverse transcribe RNAs to cDNA using PrimeScript™ RT Reagent Kit with gDNA Eraser.
Perform reverse-transcription steps as described.
Gently mix the reagent and quickly spin the samples to collect all liquid to the bottom of tubes.
Incubate the samples at 42°C for 2 min and place them at 4°C until use.
Prepare a reverse-transcription reaction mix.
Add 10 μL of mix to each reaction solution from last step.
Gently mix the reagent and quickly spin the samples to collect all liquid to the bottom of tubes.
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 15 min, 85°C for 5 s and place them at 4°C until use.
Transfer 8 μL of the mix to 96/384-well plate.
Add 2 μL of the diluted cDNA to the corresponding wells.
Seal the 96/384-well plate with an optical adhesive film.
Centrifuge the plate at 1,500 × g for 2 min at 4°C to collect all liquid to the bottom of the plate and eliminate bubbles.
Run the real-time PCR reaction with the appropriate program.
